beats.text: Your Mixture-of-Experts model is choking on its own weight, wasting 50% of your GPU memory bandwidth on redundant expert parameters.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing neural network graph where expert nodes are blinking red, indicating heavy memory traffic.

beats.text: The villain is memory traffic. During decoding, your GPU fetches massive expert weights for every token, like a runner carrying a lead backpack.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a GPU memory bus saturated with data packets, slowing down the token generation pipeline.

visual_blueprint.title: MEMORY TRAFFIC
visual_blueprint.sub: The silent killer of inference speed

motif_params.title: MEMORY TRAFFIC
motif_params.sub: The silent killer of inference speed

beats.text: Enter SlimWise: it performs prefill with the full model, then executes a seamless KV-cache handoff to a pruned, high-speed decoder.
beats.visual_focus: A clean animation showing the KV-cache object moving directly from the full model to the pruned model without re-computation.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This actually slapped. You hit the pain point immediately—everyone knows MoE models are bloated and kill VRAM. The 'lead backpack' analogy wasn't cringe, it actually helped visualize the memory bottleneck. I understood exactly what the KV-cache handoff was doing without you needing to explain it like I'm five. It felt like a real dev talking to another dev.
